card.title: Short Story 3 — A Devoted Son (Anita Desai)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The story at a glance "A Devoted Son" by Anita Desai is a story about love that becomes control without changing its name. Rakesh, the son of poor Varma, rises to the top of the medical school, honours his parents in every traditional way — marries the mother's choice, brings his bride home, touches his father's feet — and then applies his medicine to his father's life: no fried food, no sweets, tonics by the…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Rakesh's devotion turns to control — filial duty vs the father's autonomy.
Irony: the son who saved Varma's life also takes away his joys (sweets, food).

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Trick 3: The father's final act (refusing medicine, letting death come) asserts autonomy — explain what it says about dignity in old age.  ·  ## The characters worth an essay **Rakesh** is duty embodied: brilliant, obedient, grateful — and blind, in the way duty often is, to the difference between caring for a father and managing him. His flaw is not cruelty but certainty: he never doubts that he knows best, and the story's tragedy is that his certainty is medically right and personally wrong.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## The themes worth an essay **Love as control** — the central theme: care administered without consent becomes authority; the story asks where devotion ends and domination begins. **Generational reversal** — the son who owed everything now governs the man who gave everything; the pain of the story is the role reversal inside a loving family.…  ·  ## NEB short answers, solved **Q. How did Rakesh honour his parents after his success? (2 marks)** A. In every traditional way: he touched his father's feet, married a village girl of his mother's choosing instead of a foreigner, brought his bride into the family home, and cared for his parents with pride and gratitude. rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. How does Dr Rakesh's care become controlling? (2 marks) — he forbids the father's food and treats him like a patient, not a parent.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ## NEB long answers, solved **Q. "Rakesh was a devoted son, but his devotion became a cage." Discuss both sides. (8 marks)** A model answer holds the two truths in balance: on one side, the evidence of real devotion — the feet touched, the mother's choice honoured, the tireless medical care that extended the father's life; on the other, the evidence of the cage — the banned sweets, the scheduled life, the tonics…  ·  **‘A Devoted Son’ — duty vs autonomy (classified)** | Theme | Varka’s side | Varma’s side | |---|---|---| | Care | Diet, medicine, discipline | Wants taste, freedom | | Gratitude | Repay parents’ sacrifice | Gifts feel like control | | Doctor’s role | Science knows best | Son outranks father | | Love’s form | Strict regimen is love | Love is listening |

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The plot, retold with an eye on its turns The rise: Varma, a kerosene-dealer son of a poor family, announces his son's first-place result to the street; Rakesh wins a scholarship to the United States, returns with a degree and American admiration, and — the gesture the neighbourhood applauds — marries a village girl of his mother's choosing rather than an American.…  ·  ## The devices, with evidence - **Irony of the title** — the master device: "devoted son" is accurate and insufficient at once, since the devotion that feeds the father also imprisons him; the story's argument lives in that double reading.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Central irony: Rakesh's devotion (strict diet, medicine) becomes a cage for his father — love imposed becomes control; state this reversal.  ·  Trick 2: Track the power inversion: son obeyed father as a child; father must obey son in old age — structure the answer around the two halves.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. What does the father's deathbed act mean? (2 marks) — he reclaims his right to choose, dying on his own terms.
